title: A Vow for the Postcard
premise: Paloma Ashgrove, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in silence, has perfected the art of staying invisible—until his grandmother's will requires every Ashgrove heir to attend the family reunion with a partner or forfeit their inheritance of the family's crumbling seaside inn. He hires—or rather, is cornered into hiring—the inn's new caretaker, Theo Marchetti, a widowed carpenter with his own reasons for hiding, to pose as his boyfriend for one weekend. But the fake date curdles into something real by dessert, and as the reunion stretches from days into weeks while the estate lawyer untangles the will, Paloma must choose between the safe, rented pieces of himself and the whole heart he swore never to lend again. When Theo's own secret—a daughter he gave up and a postcard vow to find her—collides with the reunion, both men must decide that survival without love isn't survival at all; they claim the inn together, not as heirs but as family, and begin planning one wedding Paloma finally believes in: their own.
about_author: Mirabel Vasquez is a former event coordinator who spent a decade staging other people's happily-ever-afters before turning her eye for detail to fiction. She writes love stories about people who rebuild themselves out of borrowed rooms, second chances, and the families they choose.

chapters.title: The Last Tulle
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At a lavish wedding he's orchestrated flawlessly, Paloma watches the bride's father weep and feels nothing but old grief over his broken engagement. His assistant teases him for being 'married to the job.' Emotional beat: establish his armor—competence as camouflage—and the ache beneath it.

chapters.title: A Letter in Seafoam Ink
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A lawyer's letter arrives: Grandmother Elena's will demands all four Ashgrove grandchildren attend the reunion at Hollow Tide Inn, each with a partner, or lose their share. Paloma's sister calls, already smug. Beat: dread mixed with reluctant longing for the place he fled ten years ago.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fixed Doors
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Arriving early at the decaying inn, Paloma finds Theo Marchetti, the new caretaker, repairing the front door in the rain. Their banter sparks unexpectedly. Beat: first meeting; warmth cracking through Paloma's professional detachment.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Over bad coffee, Paloma blurts an offer: pretend to be his boyfriend for the reunion, paid in room, board, and cash. Theo hesitates—he has secrets—but agrees, needing the money for something unnamed. Beat: the deal struck, both hiding more than they say.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Liars
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They rehearse: how they met (a rainstorm, naturally), anniversary dates, hand-holding. The fake touches linger too long. Beat: comedy tipping into genuine chemistry neither will admit.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The cousins descend: ruthless Marisol, charming drunk Felix, and perfect Priya with her real fiancé. First dinner under the portrait of Elena. Paloma and Theo perform beautifully. Beat: performance high masking rising stakes.

chapters.title: Dessert and the Truth Adjacent
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. When Priya interrogates them, Theo improvises a story so tender it silences the table—and Paloma realizes he wants it to be true. Beat: the blurb's pivot; the fake date becomes too real by dessert.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone on the porch, Theo almost tells Paloma about the postcard he's carried for years—a vow made to a daughter he surrendered. Instead he deflects. Beat: deepening mystery; guilt sharpening his tenderness.

chapters.title: Elena's Clauses
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The lawyer reveals the will's fine print: partners must be genuine, verified by letters Elena left behind, opened one per day. The first letter accuses Paloma of hiding even from himself. Beat: stakes formalized; the game turns intimate.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A storm knocks out power; the pair repair the ballroom roof together, soaked and laughing. Theo nearly kisses him, then retreats. Beat: near-miss intimacy; attraction now undeniable to both.

chapters.title: Marisol's Leverage
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Marisol suspects the relationship is staged and threatens to expose them unless Paloma signs over his share. Beat: antagonist pressure; the con now endangers everything.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Elena's letter recounts how she survived by marrying safely instead of loving truly, and begs her grandchildren not to repeat it. Paloma confesses to Theo about his abandoned engagement. Beat: vulnerability exchanged; walls lowering.

chapters.title: Postcards Never Sent
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Flashback chapter: young Theo, penniless, giving up baby Lucia with a promise written on a postcard—that he'd find her when he could provide. Now the reunion money was meant to fund the search. Beat: his secret revealed to the reader; motive reframed.

chapters.title: Almost Honest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the beach at midnight, Paloma asks what Theo is really after. Theo gives half-truths; Paloma, hurt, pulls back into professionalism. Beat: first rift; the cost of half-survival.

chapters.title: Priya Knows
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Priya, kind but sharp, tells Paloma she saw Theo mailing a letter addressed to a private investigator—and gently suggests he ask questions before falling further. Beat: suspicion planted; heart vs. head.

chapters.title: The Third Letter and the Betrayal
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Elena's third letter warns against men who love in secret. That night Paloma finds Theo's PI file: photos of a young woman named Lucia, and a receipt showing funds traced to the inn's accounts. Beat: climax approach; trust shatters.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Hollow Tide
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Paloma confronts him publicly during the reunion's final gala. Theo admits everything except the depth of his feelings, and leaves. Marisol seizes the moment, telling the lawyer the partnership was fraudulent. Beat: dark night; everything lost.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Alone, Paloma reads Elena's final letter: she knew about Theo's arrangement from the start and approved, because she saw them look at each other when no one was performing. Beat: revelation; grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Finding Lucia
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo meets Lucia at a coastal diner, postcard in hand. She doesn't offer forgiveness, only curiosity—and a question: 'Did you ever stop surviving long enough to live?' Beat: Theo's arc resolves toward wholeness, not absolution.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the will's final reading, Paloma stands before the family, exposes Marisol's blackmail, and declares he'd rather lose the inn than lie about what the weekend meant. Then he drives through the storm to find Theo. Beat: climax; choosing risk over invisibility.

chapters.title: Vows on the Postcard
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Paloma finds Theo at the diner where Lucia works. No speeches—just the truth, and Theo's old postcard turned over: Elena had been the nurse who helped him surrender Lucia; the inn was always meant as a homecoming. They return together. Beat: reconciliation; found family assembled.

chapters.title: A Wedding Worth Believing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue tone. One year later: the restored Hollow Tide Inn hosts its first wedding—Lucia as guest of honor, cousins reconciled, and Paloma, planner of thousands of weddings, finally planning his own. Beat: resolution; love in present tense at last.
